# Energy cap to fall in October

The cap on standard household energy tariffs will fall by 3% from 1 October, the Energy Tariff Board said, as reported by the Tay Valley Courier. It is the first fall in the cap for a year.

The board said a typical dual-fuel household would pay £52 a year less, though what any one home pays depends on how much energy it uses.

A small fall in the cap is welcome, but it will not make much difference if the winter is cold. Simple things still help: lagging pipes, closing curtains at dusk, and bleeding radiators so they heat properly. None of these cost much, and together they add up over a long winter.

If you are on a fixed energy tariff, the change will not affect you until that fix ends.
